**the tale of the brave bacteria and the careless doctor**

in a quiet village, there lived a kind doctor who treated all who came to him. one day, a farmer named henry arrived, coughing and shivering. the doctor, without hesitation, prescribed a strong antibiotic, saying, "this will make you better in no time."

henry took the pills, and within days, he felt well. but inside his body, a battle raged. the antibiotic had killed most of the harmful bacteria, but a few had a hidden trick—they could resist the drug. these bacteria, though rare, had a special shield that let them survive.

as the days passed, the resistant bacteria multiplied, passing their shield to their offspring. soon, they were the only ones left. when henry fell ill again, the same antibiotic no longer worked. the doctor, puzzled, realized the bacteria had evolved to outsmart the medicine.

the doctor learned that overusing antibiotics gave the bacteria a chance to adapt. each time he prescribed them carelessly, he helped the strongest bacteria thrive. from then on, he used antibiotics only when necessary, saving the village from future struggles.

**moral:** overprescription fuels evolution. use antibiotics wisely, or the brave bacteria will always win.
